narrative: High ticket volume with mostly fast fixes (1-2 days), but the final three tickets in March 2025 show a cascading, unresolved chain: the API 'still not fully resolved' after a fix ('please keep this open until it's fully sorted'), then the ERP connector failing 'since this week's API patch.' The customer's requests escalate in sophistication across the year, from 'please look at the whole account, not just this one ticket' to 'can someone look at the whole pipeline together?' Individual symptoms get patched quickly, but the pattern of one fix breaking the next component is worsening, not improving.

The same handful of bugs — export corruption, dashboard outages, report-builder formatting resets, missed alerts — repeat on a cycle across 18 months, each time closed as resolved and each time returning: export corruption comes back 'for a third time this year' with the customer asking 'what's actually different about our export versus others,' dashboard tiles fail with 'same pattern as last August,' and formatting resets prompt 'this is now the third ticket on the same bug since October.' No ticket in the record shows a genuine root-cause fix, and the tone shifts from reporting problems to open skepticism that fixes ever hold.

Started as routine UI and admin questions but escalated into serious data-integrity incidents: all 14 configured alerts vanished ('they don't appear to have been deleted — they're gone from the list entirely'), and scheduled exports silently show 'completed' with no output file, forcing a manual workaround the customer calls 'not sustainable.' The most recent export ticket is explicitly unresolved ('need a fix that actually holds'), and alerts failed again after an August migration. Low ticket count masks a real reliability problem in the two modules this account depends on operationally.

A technically engaged account raising specific, well-documented bugs (API pagination duplicates, intermittent connector failures) in a calm, collaborative tone, including offering logs and reproduction detail unprompted. One real limitation remains open — API timeouts on queries over 12 months of data, left unresolved with no follow-up — but there is no urgency or frustration in the language, just steady technical dialogue. Resolution times run long (up to 14 days) without any complaint about speed.

A genuine turnaround: months of accumulating problems (an unresolved new-hire login, an export that failed 'four Mondays in a row' then failed again after being called resolved) culminated in an explicit escalation demand — 'I'm not confident anyone actually owns this account's problems end to end. Please have someone senior call me.' After an account review call in September the tone flips decisively: 'feels like we're finally getting somewhere,' 'exports have been reliable since last week, thank you,' followed by a run of small, low-stakes asks marked 'no rush.' This is a saved relationship rather than a clean history, but the current trajectory is clearly positive.
Two straightforward technical tickets eight months apart, both resolved without complaint. Nothing in volume or tone suggests any relationship risk.

Sparse, entirely positive contact spread across 18 months — a webhook question, a feature request, an embedding question — each closed with explicit thanks ('exactly what we needed,' 'nice experience overall'). A textbook healthy, low-touch account.

Low-frequency, factual tickets — rate limits, alert routing, a missing export column, connector setup, threshold tuning — spread over 15 months with no urgency or repeated complaints. An early rate-limit question was never explicitly closed out but also never resurfaced as a complaint. Reads as a stable, unremarkable account.

Went through a sustained crisis from mid-2024 through mid-2025 — recurring API outages, dashboard failures lasting 'three weeks,' and an explicit escalation ('this needs to go beyond first-line support... please escalate') after the customer said the pattern was undermining trust in the numbers. From July 2025 the tone reverses decisively: 'the dashboard fix... has held up well,' 'dashboards have been solid for a couple of weeks straight,' and by October the customer is 'comfortable expanding usage again' with a new API integration. The crisis was real but the account's own words track a genuine recovery.

Four widely-spaced onboarding and admin requests over 16 months (connector mapping, API access, CRM re-sync, new-hire setup), all resolved without friction. A healthy, low-touch account with no complaint language anywhere.
Three routine administrative tickets over a year — alert recipient updates, a threshold-sync bug, temporary auditor access — each closed cleanly with no frustration or recurrence.

A steady trickle of small, mostly alert-related bugs (a holiday-period alert that never fired, recipients not receiving emails, alerts arriving 20-30 minutes late) plus report-builder permission and export-button glitches, none accompanied by frustration language. Two threads remain open at the point of last contact — the holiday alert failure and a per-user export-button bug — showing the alerts module in particular carries several small unresolved items even though nothing here reads as urgent.
Two administrative tickets — sync frequency question, seat reallocation for a reorg — resolved without incident. No signal of risk.

The same failures recur every few months despite fast individual fixes: the ERP/Netvisor connector goes down repeatedly ('feels like we're back here every couple of months — can this get a permanent fix instead of a patch?'), and report builder crashes on four separate occasions across the year, often stacked with other outages the same day ('third thing broken today — can someone actually call me?'). Tickets close in 1-2 days each time, but nothing suggests a root cause was ever addressed, and the tone hardens over the year from inconvenience to pointed distrust.

Modest ticket volume, but the two most recent issues are unresolved: a scheduled export that silently failed to send, and dashboard slowness that resurfaced in August after supposedly being fixed in June — 'the dashboard loading issue from June is back... could this be looked at properly this time?' That phrasing signals the customer already doubts the fix will stick, and the visible history closes on that open, skeptical note.

Calm, factual bug reports across five different modules over seven months, each resolved within a week. The most recent ticket — intermittent SSO login failures, with the customer noting their own IT 'has checked our side and it looks clean' — is left unresolved with no follow-up, a live access issue at the end of the visible history.

Low volume but a textbook slow-burn risk. A connector double-sync noticed in January ('I'd like to understand why before assuming it's harmless') was still happening in March, now producing duplicate rows that required manually rebuilding a month's figures in Excel — the earlier fix did not hold. By June, after an alert threshold silently reset itself, the customer reports they've started keeping their own spreadsheet of alert and connector settings 'to spot this kind of drift ourselves,' adding 'no need to prioritise this one specifically.' The tone never rises above calm and professional, but the account is quietly building workarounds around the product instead of trusting it — exactly the pattern most likely to precede a quiet non-renewal.

Chronic, high-frequency instability across nearly every module, consistently timed around board reporting ('of course it's the week before the board meeting. This module has been a recurring problem all year'). Report builder crashes recur across four separate months, seat allocation breaks twice ('same seat allocation problem as January is back'), and a single stretch in August 2025 produces five tickets in three days spanning seats, connectors, exports and dashboards together. Despite each ticket closing in 1-2 days, there is no evidence of a lasting fix for any recurring failure, and repeated requests for 'a proper root cause, not another quick patch' go unanswered in the text.

Sparse, low-urgency contact almost entirely about feature gaps rather than defects — bulk provisioning, webhook schema, and a rolling 12-month average the report builder doesn't support natively. The customer is still working around the missing formula manually four months after first asking ('still working around it manually on our end. Any update on the roadmap?'), a mild but real sign of patience wearing on one specific gap; otherwise the tone stays professional and undemanding.
Two isolated, resolved tickets eight months apart — a pagination bug and an alert-recipient question — with no complaint language. Nothing here suggests risk.
